lines.japanese: ガツーンって来た。
lines.english: It hit me with a WHAM.

lines.japanese: 「ぅぅ……ぃ、あぅぅ……」
lines.english: “Uhh... ngh... ahh...”

lines.japanese: 全しんにガツーンって来た。
lines.english: It hit my whole body with a WHAM.

lines.japanese: 夢テレビで味わう偽モンとは全ぜんちがった、本モンの音とかニオイとか寒さとか。そうゆう「体がある」ってなつかしい感かくが、全しんにガツーンってきた。
lines.english: Real sounds and smells and cold—nothing like the fake ones on dream TV. That long-forgotten feeling of having a body hit every bit of me with a WHAM.

lines.japanese: ……ガツーン？　うーん、やっぱゴズゥーンかもしんない。どっちでもいっか。
lines.english: ...A wham? Hmm. Maybe it was more of a ker-WHUMP. Ah, who cares.

lines.japanese: 本モンの世界はまぶしかったけど、でも来ちったもんはしょーがーないから、とりあいずおれ、がんばって目ぇあけた。
lines.english: The real world was bright, but, well, I was already here, so no helping it. For now, I tried real hard to open my eyes.

lines.japanese: そしたらおれの体は、なんかアタマがぐったりしてて、おでこがテーブルにくっついてたから、ゆっくりおこしてみた。
lines.english: My body was slumped over the table, my forehead pressed against the wood. Slowly, I lifted my head.

lines.japanese: 「ぃ、ぃつ、つ……」
lines.english: “N-ngh... ow...”

lines.japanese: ゆっくり動かしたのに、久しぶりだったから、首とかがギシギシゆって、ちょっと痛かった。あと忘れてたけど、アタマは思ったよりか重かった。
lines.english: I moved really slowly, but it had been so long that my neck and stuff creaked, and it hurt a little. Also, I'd forgotten a head was heavier than you'd think.

lines.japanese: さいしょはまぶしくて目ぇショボショボしたけど、まわりをキョロキョロ見てるうちにすぐなれた。
lines.english: The light made my eyes sting at first, but after I spent a little while looking all around, they got used to it.

lines.japanese: いかにも本モンって感じの、ハッキリ見えすぎるけしきだった。でんきの明かりは明るすぎるし、テレビの声だって聞こえすぎる。
lines.english: Everything looked too clear—like it was shouting that it was real. The electric lights were too bright, and even the voices on TV were too loud.

lines.japanese: こっちの世界は何でもハッキリしすぎてる。もちょっと暗くしたり、もちょっとボンヤリさした方が、なにかとイイのにって思う。
lines.english: Everything in this world was too clear. I thought all kinds of things would be better if they made it a little darker and a little blurrier.

lines.japanese: あ、そうだ。そんなことより、うーん、おれはどうやってあっちのせかいに帰ればいいのかな……。
lines.english: Oh, right. More important than that—hmm. How was I supposed to get back to the other world...?

lines.japanese: 「ぁー、ぁァー、ぁィぅえをー」
lines.english: “Ahh... aaah... ah-ee-oo-eh-oh.”

lines.japanese: とりあいず、体を持つ感かくは久しぶりだったから、声を出したり手ぇ動かすれんしゅうをしてみた。
lines.english: It'd been a long time since I felt what having a body was like, so I practiced making sounds and moving my hands.

lines.japanese: 「ん、んんっ……あィウェオー……あい、うぇおー……あい、うえお……」
lines.english: “Mm, mmm... ah-ee-weh-oh... ah-ee, weh-oh... ah-ee, oo-eh-oh...”

lines.japanese: れんしゅうしながらテレビを見た。ちょうど本モンのテレビがついてて、アニメの番ぐみやってた。
lines.english: I watched TV while I practiced. A real television happened to be on, showing a cartoon.

lines.japanese: おー！　これおぼえてる、なつかしいアニメだ。
lines.english: Oh! I remembered this one. Man, I hadn't seen this cartoon in forever.

lines.japanese: でもちょっと見てたら、すげー話が分かりやすくてビックリしちった。だって、へんなアタマしたおばちゃんが買いもの行くんでおもてに出たけど、サイフわすれててアラヤダとかゆうの。
lines.english: But after I watched for a bit, I couldn't believe how easy the story was to understand. This funny-haired lady goes out shopping, except she forgets her purse and goes, ‘Oh, silly me!’

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、くふふ」
lines.english: “Heh... heh heh.”

lines.japanese: おれ思わずわらっちった。こうゆうフツーなの、なつかしい。
lines.english: I laughed without meaning to. I'd missed normal stuff like this.

lines.japanese: そういえば、向こうの夢テレビでも、さいしょはこうゆうフツーの番ぐみやってた気ぃする。うん、そうだ、ずーっと再ほう送してるうちにあちこちカットされて、だんだんヘンなふうになってったんだ。
lines.english: Come to think of it, dream TV used to show normal programs like this too. Yeah, that was it. But they got rerun forever, and bits and pieces kept getting cut, so little by little they turned weird.

lines.japanese: 夢テレビもＤＪコンドルもガルーダも、みんなそうやって、ちょっとずつオカシクなっちゃった。
lines.english: Dream TV, DJ Condor, Garuda—they all went weird that way, little by little.

lines.japanese: ずっとあっちにいると、みんなそうなっちゃうのかもしんない。おれはオカシクなんないで超よかった。だから、はやく帰りたいな。
lines.english: Maybe that's what happens to everybody who stays over there too long. I was super glad I hadn't gotten weird. So I wanted to hurry back.
“Sigh...”

lines.japanese: そんで、へんなアタマのおばちゃんとか、へんなアタマのおばちゃんの弟とか、へんなアタマのおばちゃんのお父さんとか見てたら、なんだかだんだんヤな気ぶんになってきちった。
lines.english: But as I watched the weird-headed lady, and the weird-headed lady's little brother, and the weird-headed lady's father, I slowly started feeling bad.

lines.japanese: 「あーあ……あしたは学校かあ……」
lines.english: “Awww... School tomorrow...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのっ、いたみさん」
lines.english: “U-um, Mr. Itami?”

lines.japanese: 「あい？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: うしろにだれか来たみたいだ。もう体はちゃんと動かせるようになったから、なんだろうと思ってギギギィーって振りむいてみた。
lines.english: Somebody had come up behind me. My body was working properly now, so I wondered who it was and creaked around to look.

lines.japanese: 「お、おふろ、沸いたん、ですっ……けどっ」
lines.english: “Th-the bath is ready... but...”

lines.japanese: なんか入口に、おれより上の学年っぽい女子が立ってた。おっかながってるみたいに、ビクビクした目ぇでおれんコト見てる。だれだろう、このおねーちゃん。どっかで見たことある気ぃする。
lines.english: There was this girl at the door who looked like she was in a grade above me. She was looking at me with these all-scared, twitchy eyes. Who was this big girl? Felt like I'd seen her someplace before.
“Hmm?”
“Hmmm?”

lines.japanese: 思いだそうとしてジーッと見てたら、おねーちゃんモジモジ下向いてカオかくしちゃった。
lines.english: I stared at her, trying to remember. The girl fidgeted, looked down, and hid her face.

lines.japanese: 「お、おふろ……なんですけど、つ、使い方、分かりますか……」
lines.english: “The bath... Um, do you know how to use it...?”

lines.japanese: 「おふろ？」
lines.english: “The bath?”

lines.japanese: おふろ。おふろ。おふろ。
lines.english: The bath. The bath. The bath.

lines.japanese: あー、フロかあ！　なつかしいなあ。向こうでは体よごれねっから、おふろなんか入らないだで、おれ、すっかり忘れちってたよ。
lines.english: Oh, right—a bath! I hadn't thought about those in forever. My body didn't get dirty over there, so I never took baths. I'd completely forgotten about them.

lines.japanese: そっか、こっちではおふろに入んないと体ばっちくなって、かゆくなったり、くさくなったりすんだよね。
lines.english: Yeah, in this world, if you don't take baths, your body gets all dirty and itchy and smelly.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: そんで、思わず自分の体みて気が付いた。なんかおれ、服とかすげー汚れてんの。血ぃとかドロとかが付いてて、赤かったり黒かったりすんの。
lines.english: Then I happened to look down at my body and noticed something. My clothes were super dirty. They had blood and mud and stuff on them, all red and black.

lines.japanese: 「ええー！　っだよこれー、ふーざけー、超きったねーじゃんかー」
lines.english: “What the heck is this? You've gotta be kidding! I'm crazy filthy!”

lines.japanese: 「やっべー、もー、またお母さんに怒らいちゃうよー」
lines.english: “Aw, crap. Mom's gonna get mad at me again.”

lines.japanese: だからおれマッハで立って、そいから上の服ぬごうとした。
lines.english: So I jumped up at Mach speed and started taking off my shirt.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、あ、あの、伊丹さん──」
lines.english: “What? U-um, Mr. Itami—”

lines.japanese: そしたらあのおねーちゃんが、なんかアタフタあわてだした。
lines.english: Then the girl started getting all flustered.

lines.japanese: 「──じゃ、ない？　の？　あれ？　誰ですか？」
lines.english: “—you're... not him? Huh? Who are you?”

lines.japanese: 「あい？　なにがあ？」
lines.english: “Huh? What're you talking about?”

lines.japanese: ぷあーって服から首を出して、ねーちんのほうを見た。そしたら、
lines.english: I popped my head out through my shirt and looked at the girl. And then—

lines.japanese: 「ありっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: そのカオ、やっぱ知ってるカオな気ぃがした。
lines.english: That face. I really did feel like I knew it.

lines.japanese: 「ありり？　おまい、もしかしてポッポ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Hey, are you Poppo?”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「ポッポでしょ？　おーっ、ポッポだよね？」
lines.english: “You're Poppo, right? Oh! You are Poppo!”

lines.japanese: そうだ、うん、なんかもう子どもじゃなくなってるけど、このおねーちゃんはお姉ちゃんじゃなくて、おれの妹だ。
lines.english: Yeah, that was it. She wasn't a little kid anymore, and even if she looked older than me, she wasn't my big sister. She was my little sister.

lines.japanese: 「うっわあ、なんだよおまい、もぉー！　そんな背ぇのびちゃってえー！」
lines.english: “Whoa! Look at you! When'd you get so tall?”

lines.japanese: おれは手ぇのばして、小ばとの頭をポンポンたたいた。久しぶりに妹に会えて、もうおれ、うれしゲロはきそうだった。
lines.english: I reached out and patted Kobato on the head. I was so happy to see my little sister again I almost puked for joy.

lines.japanese: でも小ばとは、ポンポンされながらポケーッて固まっちゃった。
lines.english: But Kobato just stood there in a daze while I patted her.

lines.japanese: 「おいぃー、どしたポッポー。ちょびっと会わねーうちに、兄ちゃんの顔わすれちったんかあ？」
lines.english: “Hey, what's wrong, Poppo? I go away for a little while and you forget your big brother's face?”
“Huh...? Big... Brother...?”

lines.japanese: 小ばとのあごが下がって、目ん玉が上がった。
lines.english: Kobato's jaw dropped and her eyes lifted.

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ、兄ちゃんだよ。羽田ようじにきまってんだろモォー」
lines.english: “Yeah, your big brother. Yoji Haneda, obviously. Come on, Poppo.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　えっ、なんで？　えっ、えっ？」
lines.english: “What? Huh? Why? What? What?”

lines.japanese: おれもおどろいたけど、小ばとはもっとおどろいてて、まん丸い目ぇを上から下にクリクリさせた。
lines.english: I was surprised, but Kobato was even more surprised. Her big round eyes rolled over me from top to bottom.

lines.japanese: 「え？　え？　えっ、うそっ、お兄ちゃんなの？」
lines.english: “What? What? Wait—are you really my brother?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、そうだってゆってんじゃん、もーポッポはぁー。おまい、ちゃんといい子にしてたかぁ？」
lines.english: “I keep telling you I am. Jeez, Poppo. Have you been a good girl?”

lines.japanese: 「ほ、ほんと……？　ほんとに……？」
lines.english: “R-really...? Is it really...?”

lines.japanese: なんか小ばとのほっぺがヒクヒクして、口がフルフルして、目ぇがウルウルしてきた。
lines.english: Kobato's cheeks started twitching. Her mouth trembled, and her eyes welled up.

lines.japanese: 「ほんとに、ほんとの……お兄ちゃん……？」
lines.english: “Are you really... my real brother...?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ほんとだよ、いのちかけてもいいよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, really. I'd bet my life on it.”

lines.japanese: 小ばとの声はユラユラしてて聞こえにくかった。でもおれは久しぶりに妹に会えたのがうれしーくて、かってにカオがニコニコしてきちった。
lines.english: Kobato's voice wobbled so much it was hard to hear. But I was so happy to see my little sister again that my face broke into a grin all by itself.

lines.japanese: 「お、おにっ、おにっ……」
lines.english: “B-Big... Big...”

lines.japanese: 小ばとも超うれしそうにかおクシャクシャにしながら、すんっ、すんっ、て鼻すすって、
lines.english: Kobato scrunched her face up like she was super happy too and sniffled, sniff, sniff.

lines.japanese: 「えふっ、えっ、えっ、え、え、え……」
lines.english: “Hh... eh... eh... eh, eh, eh...”

lines.japanese: 肩ゆらしながらちょっとずつアタマ下向いてって、
lines.english: Her shoulders shook, and little by little her head sank.

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃあーん……」
lines.english: “Big Brotheeer...”

lines.japanese: そんで両方の手ぇ、まぶたに持ってって、グジュグジュ泣きだした。
lines.english: Then she put both hands to her eyes and started bawling.

lines.japanese: 「な、なーに？　どしたポッポ、ぽんぽん痛いのー？」
lines.english: “Wh-what? What's wrong, Poppo? Does your tummy hurt?”

lines.japanese: おれ超あせって、妹の肩つかんでしゃがんだ。小ばとは目ぇゴシゴシしながら、首ブンブンよこにふった。
lines.english: I panicked, grabbed my sister by the shoulders, and crouched down. Kobato rubbed her eyes and shook her head hard from side to side.

lines.japanese: 「お、おかっ、おかえりなさい……」
lines.english: “W-wel... welcome home...”

lines.japanese: 「ポッポ、あいさつなんかいいから。ぽんぽん痛くないの？」
lines.english: “Poppo, forget the greeting. Your tummy doesn't hurt?”

lines.japanese: 「ひっ……ひく……」
もっかい聞いたら、こんどは首たてにうんうんふった。
lines.english: When I asked again, she nodded her head up and down this time.

lines.japanese: 「そっか、痛くないのね。あーよかった、あんま兄ちゃんおどかすなよー、もぉー」
lines.english: “Oh, good. It doesn't hurt. Don't scare your big brother like that, come on.”

lines.japanese: 「おかえり……お帰りなさい、お帰りなさい……」
lines.english: “Welcome home... Welcome home. Welcome home...”

lines.japanese: なんか小ばと泣いてるけど、いちようよろこんでるみたいだ。
lines.english: Kobato was crying, but she seemed happy, I guess.

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “Y-yeah.”

lines.japanese: だからおれ、ちょっと困っちった。
lines.english: So I didn't know what to do.

lines.japanese: だってよろこばれたって、おれ、すぐ帰るつもりなのに。
lines.english: 'Cause she was so happy, but I was planning to go back right away.

lines.japanese: 小ばとに会えたのは良かったし、本モンのテレビも楽しいからもっと見たかった。でもやっぱ、こっちに長くいたら、またぜってーヤなこととか起こるじゃんか。
lines.english: I was glad I got to see Kobato, and real TV was fun, so I wanted to watch more. But if I stayed in this world too long, something bad was definitely gonna happen again.

lines.japanese: だからおれ、わりいけど、帰る方法が分かったらすぐ帰るよ。
lines.english: So, sorry and all, but once I figured out how to go back, I was leaving right away.

lines.japanese: 「えへ……おにいちゃん、戻ってきた……えへへ……」
lines.english: “Heh... My brother came back... Heh heh...”

lines.japanese: でも小ばとが真っ赤な目ぇグジグジこすりながら俺んこと見て、うれしそうな声でゆってっから……。
lines.english: But Kobato rubbed at her red, soggy eyes, looked at me, and said it in such a happy voice...

lines.japanese: だからおれ、すぐ帰るとか言いだしにくくって、どうすっかなあとか超なやんじって、だからとりあいず小ばとに返事だけしといた。
lines.english: That made it hard to tell her I was going right back. I worried like crazy about what to do, so for now I just answered her.

lines.japanese: 「うん……ただいまポッポ……」
lines.english: “Yeah... I'm home, Poppo...”

lines.japanese: 「えへっ、えっ、えっ、え、え、え……」
lines.english: “Heh... eh... eh... eh, eh, eh...”

lines.japanese: そしたら小ばと、また肩ヒクヒクさして下向いちゃった。
lines.english: Then Kobato's shoulders started shaking again, and she looked down.

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃぁぁぁん……」
lines.english: “Big Brotheeeer...”

lines.japanese: あ。
lines.english: Ah.

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃぁぁぁん……」
lines.english: “Big Brotheeeer...”

lines.japanese: なんかそんとき、おれアッとか思って、アッ昔にもこんなことあったかもしんないって思った。
lines.english: Right then, something in me went, Oh. Maybe something like this had happened once a long time ago too.

lines.japanese: 「おにいちゃん……ぐすん、ひっく……」
lines.english: “Big Brother... sniff, hic...”

lines.japanese: おかしいよね。だっておれ、向こうの世界にすっこんでるときは、ほとんど昔のことなんて思いだしたりしないじゃんか。
lines.english: It's weird. When I'm holed up in the other world, I hardly ever remember anything from long ago.

lines.japanese: でもなんか、なんでか知んないけど、いまはつい昔のこといきなし思いだしちゃった。ヘンなの。
lines.english: But now, I dunno why, the past suddenly came back all at once. Weird.

lines.japanese: あ、べつにヘンじゃねっか。昔のこと思いだすなんて、こっちにいればフツーのことだっけ。
lines.english: Oh. Maybe it wasn't weird. Remembering the past was normal when you were in this world, wasn't it?

lines.japanese: あー、そっかー。
lines.english: Oh. Right.

lines.japanese: やだなー。昔のことなんか思いださないほうが楽しいのに。
lines.english: Aw, man. It was more fun not remembering the past.

lines.japanese: 小ばとがしくしく泣いてた。
lines.english: Kobato was crying softly.

lines.japanese: だからおれ、小ばとを守ってやんなきゃって思ったんだ。
lines.english: And I thought I had to protect her.

lines.japanese: 小ばとを助けんのは、おれのやく目だ。だっておれは兄ちゃんだし、兄ちゃんはいもうとを助けるものだって、やさしいほうのお母さんがゆってた。
lines.english: Helping Kobato was my job. I was her big brother, and the nice Mom had told me big brothers were supposed to help their little sisters.

lines.japanese: だからおれは、何回もこわいほうのお母さんにおねがいしたんだ。
lines.english: So I begged the scary Mom over and over.

lines.japanese: 小ばとんコトいじめないで。そんかし、おれんコトいっぱいいじめていいから。
lines.english: Don't pick on Kobato. You can pick on me all you want instead.

lines.japanese: だからおれは、まだ年少さんだった小ばとをひっしこいてかばって、何発もぶたれたり何発もけっとばされたりした。
lines.english: So I tried as hard as I could to shield Kobato, who was still only in the youngest preschool class, and I got hit and kicked over and over.

lines.japanese: そしたらある日、おれは痛くて恐くて悔しくて、なんかだんだんムカついてきて……頭クラーってしてきて……目のまえサーって赤くなってきたんだー。
lines.english: Then one day, it hurt and I was scared and frustrated, and I got madder and madder... My head went woozy... Everything in front of me washed red.

lines.japanese: ほら、フツーだれでもみんな、ムカつくことあると頭クラーってなって目のまえサーって赤くなるじゃんか。そこまではべつにフツーのことじゃんか。
lines.english: See, whenever anybody gets really mad, their head goes woozy and everything washes red. That much is totally normal.

lines.japanese: でもおれの場合そんだけじゃなくて、もっとムカついちゃうとキューっておなか痛くなって、ウェーってゲロ出そうになんの。だからそんときも、おれムカつきすぎちゃってウェーってなってたの。
lines.english: But with me, there was more. If I got even madder, my stomach cramped up and I felt like I was gonna puke. So that time I got so mad I started gagging.

lines.japanese: そんで、やっぱ目のまえはいつもみたくサーって赤くなってたんだけど、そんときはなんか台所の包丁だけがギンギラギンに光ってて、おれそれ見て一しゅん「いいもん見っけー」って思ったのね。
lines.english: Everything in front of me had washed red like always, except the kitchen knife was glittering like crazy. For just a second, I looked at it and thought, Hey, found something good.

lines.japanese: でもそんとき、ちょうどお母さんの必殺キックがさくれつして、おれドカーッてカベまでブッとばされちったんよ。首グキーって曲がって、いってーえ、もう肩にくっつきそうんなっちったで。
lines.english: But right then, Mom unleashed her finishing-move kick and sent me flying clear across the room into the wall. My neck bent with a nasty wrench. It hurt so bad my head nearly touched my shoulder.

lines.japanese: そんでおれ超痛くって、一しゅんカチーンと来ちって、そしたらおれ……あの、なんだっけ……えーっと、だから……。
lines.english: It hurt so much that for a second I got really mad, and then I... Um, what happened...? Let's see, so then...

lines.japanese: だから……あれ？
lines.english: So then... Huh?

lines.japanese: んー、あれ、どしたんだっけ。
lines.english: Hmm. What happened after that?

lines.japanese: うーん、なーんだあ、やっぱ思いだせないや。
lines.english: Huh. Guess I still can't remember.

lines.japanese: まあ分かんねーけど、気ぃついたらおれ、小ばとに泣きながらおかえりってゆわれてたの。
lines.english: Well, I dunno. But the next thing I knew, Kobato was crying and telling me welcome home.

lines.japanese: こんなふうに──
lines.english: Just like this—

lines.japanese: ──いまみたく。
lines.english: —just like now.

lines.japanese: 「えへ、ぐすっ……おかえりお兄ちゃん……」
lines.english: “Heh... sniff... Welcome home, Big Brother...”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “Y-yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「おに、お兄ちゃんもごはん食べる？　もう私、おままごとの砂ごはんじゃなくて、ほんとのごはん作れるんだよ、ぐす、えへへ……」
lines.english: “B-Big Brother, do you want something to eat too? I can make real food now, not pretend dinners out of sand. Sniff... heh heh...”

lines.japanese: 小ばとは泣きながらウキウキしてた。
lines.english: Kobato was crying and bubbling over with excitement at the same time.

lines.japanese: でもおれは、いつ「すぐ帰ります」ってゆおうか超なやんでた。
lines.english: But I was worrying like crazy about when to tell her, ‘I'm going back right away.’
